subject: physics
question_text: State the vector form of Newton’s law of gravitation.

verification.note: The mark split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The vector form
lines: For two point masses m₁ and m₂ whose
separation vector is r, of magnitude r,
Dividing by r³ rather than r² supplies the
direction, since r itself has length r.
steps.why: The r³ is not a different law — it is r²  with one extra r used to turn the vector r into a direction.
common_mistakes: Writing r² in the denominator with the vector r on top, which gets the magnitude wrong by a factor r.

recall.must_convey: That F equals minus G m one m two by r cubed, times the vector r.
accept: minus G m one m two by r cubed times r

steps.label: What the sign means

lines.text: The minus sign means the force is attractive

lines: F points opposite to r, that is back towards
the other mass. The scalar form G m₁m₂/r²
gives only the size, never the direction.
steps.why: The Fastrack omits the minus sign; NCERT keeps it, and without it the formula describes a force that pushes the masses apart. Write the minus.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign, which turns gravitation into a repulsion.

recall.must_convey: That the minus sign means the force is attractive, pointing back towards the other mass.
reject: minus G m one m two by r cubed
